newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jewish group asks France to tour Nazi-era art.
newsitem.headline: Jewish group asks France to tour Nazi-era art.

text.p: The anti-Nazi Simon Wiesenthal Centre said on Monday it had asked France to send some of the 2,000 art works recovered from Germany after the war on a world tour to help their original owners identify and claim them.

Wiesenthal officials met with an advisor to President Jacques Chirac in February to propose an international tour of the works, some of which are believed to have been looted by the Nazis from Jewish families, the Centre said in a statement.

The officials suggested the exhibit's first stop be the Centre's Museum of Tolerance in Los Angeles to "permit Holocaust survivors in the United States the opportunity to verify potential claims to these pieces," it said.

France, seeking to disprove charges it was still holding artworks seized by the occupying forces, will unveil this week exhibits in five French museums of 987 paintings, drawings and sculptures that have not been reclaimed by the families or heirs of their original owners.

The decision to hold the exhibits came on the heels of a report by the Cour des Comptes, France's state auditing body, accusing France's state-run museums of failing in their duty to seek out the owners or heirs of some 1995 works of art in their possession since the end of the war.
